name: I Iso Left
purpose: The same isolation block the other way. The flanker stays where he is, so this runs away from our strength — which is exactly why it is open.

RE.rule: Cut off pursuit from behind. You are the last one to the ball, so never quit on the play.

RT.rule: The tackle is on your inside shoulder. Get your head across him and wall him off so he cannot chase.

RG.rule: Nobody is over you. Step back inside and cut off anyone chasing through the middle.

C.rule: You have the nose, head up on you. Hands inside and do not let him cross your face to the playside.

LG.rule: The tackle sits in the gap outside you. You and our tackle double him — hands inside, drive him backwards.

LT.rule: Double the tackle on your inside shoulder with the guard. Drive him back, and if the middle linebacker runs through, the guard comes off onto him.

LE.rule: The end is head up on you. Drive him out and widen the hole.

Z.rule: Come across behind the line and cut off anybody chasing from the backside.

QB.rule: Reverse pivot and hand the ball to the tailback at four yards. Then clear out and fake wide.

FB.rule: Lead through the hole and put your facemask on the linebacker sitting over the double team. Move him any direction — just move him.

TB.rule: Take the handoff at four yards, get downhill behind the fullback, and cut off his block.

coaching_points: Running away from the flanker means one fewer blocker out there, so the tailback has to get north fast.
Their defense will usually shade toward our flanker. That is the reason this play exists — check it before you call it.
Same block, same read as I Iso Right. Do not teach it as a new play, teach it as the same play flipped.
